bet: The Hungarian algorithm finds a maximum-weight perfect matching in the bipartite representation, which corresponds to a 2-regular subgraph (union of cycles) that maximizes the number of original graph edges used. Breaking these cycles yields long paths that greedy methods miss because they get stuck in local minima. This is a fundamentally different search strategy that can find longer paths by exploiting the global structure of the graph rather than local greedy choices.
